summary.headline: EIH Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 16%, EBITDA up 19%, PAT up 21% to ₹153 cr as RevPAR grew ~18% on ARR gains.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as a good quarter, with consolidated revenue up 16% YoY, EBITDA up 19% and net PAT of ₹153 cr versus ₹142 cr a year earlier. Industry occupancy rose 1-3% and ARR 8-10%, and EIH's RGI improved from 121% to 130%. Renovations at Mumbai hotels cut inventory and pulled occupancy down to 71% from 74% on total rooms, while ARR growth drove RevPAR up 18.3%. Cash reserves stayed above ₹1,100 cr, with H1 capex of roughly ₹400 cr largely offset by operating cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹142 cr last year (+21% YoY as stated)

financial_highlights.metric: Owned hotels RevPAR on reduced inventory

segments.name: Oberoi brand (luxury)
segments.commentary: Q2 RevPAR up 20.9% vs luxury segment 18.2%; YTD growth in line with industry, held back by renovation key closures in Q1 and Q2.

segments.name: Trident brand (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: Q2 RevPAR up 14.8% vs upper upscale segment 10.1%; Trident outgrew the segment on YTD basis as well.

segments.name: International hotels
segments.commentary: Mauritius occupancy rose to about 67% after UK travel restrictions lifted in early Q2; Indonesia, Egypt and Marrakesh also performed well.

segments.name: OFS / other commercial income
segments.commentary: OFS revenue ₹150 cr in Q2, up ~20% YoY; management said OFS and commercial income grew slower than rooms, lowering overall revenue growth to 16% vs RevPAR 18%.

segments.name: Oberoi Rajgarh (new)
segments.commentary: In first full season, hotel performing ahead of management expectations; Q1 was EBITDA negative due to flight suspension from 15 April, and management expects EBITDA-positive in Q3.

guidance_outlook: Management expects good Q3 and Q4 if no unknown global events occur, citing healthy foreign bookings and strong domestic hotel demand.
Mumbai and most renovations are complete; Bangalore renovation (18 keys at a time) is ongoing, and room renovations are planned for summer months, not Q3/Q4.
Oberoi Mumbai F&B/spa/gym renovation to reopen in January; management expects better room revenue growth in H2.
Pipeline: about 1,100 owned keys by 2030 (incl. ~7.63 lakh sq ft Bangalore commercial space); about 1,893 managed keys by 2031.
Oberoi Grand renovation timeline unchanged; reopening referenced to September (per stock exchange disclosure).
Tirupati greenfield delayed due to land allocation change; London under construction; Goa design in final stages awaiting approvals; Hebbal (Bangalore) ground-breaking planned for calendar 2027.
Wildflower Hall (Shimla) contract revenue booking expected from end of Q4; revenue share of 47.1% to state government.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex mainly for Hyderabad land (just under 10 acres, freehold, ~300-key Trident planned), Oberoi Grand renovation and Mumbai renovations; cash from operations offset it, leaving a very small dilution in funds.
Oberoi Grand (heritage) renovation underway with larger rooms and lower room count; public areas being fully renovated.
Bangalore Hebbal project: two hotels plus commercial and retail, ~1.7 million sq ft; ground-breaking early calendar 2027. Management declined to disclose project cost.
Bhubaneswar land bank: expansion plans in planning stage, not started; Bhubaneswar is not an EIH hotel.
Hyderabad Raidurg Oberoi (management contract with Prestige) and Trident Hi-Tech City hotel to open within a two-year commitment window.
demand_pricing: Q2 industry occupancy up 1-3% and ARR up 8-10% YoY; domestic air traffic contracted on higher airfares while hotel demand stayed buoyant.
BRICS summit boosted NCR ARR in September; Jaipur and Ranthambore benefited from Vanyavilas open for 2 of 3 closure months plus off-season rate push at Rajvilas.
MICE share of room nights rose to 16% from 12%; direct segment fell to 45% from 48%.
Management reported encouraging foreign booking revival, with growth expected to be healthier in Q3; single-digit RevPAR growth in Bangalore and Chennai flagged by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue (16%) grow slower than RevPAR (18%+) despite MICE pickup, and what was F&B growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said business mix was the cause: OFS and other commercial income grew less than rooms. OFS was ₹150 cr, up ~20%; F&B growth figure was not given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 finance cost elevated?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was a one-time settlement of prior-period lease rental at Oberoi Delhi after a lease cost increase; expected to normalise in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will renovation drag ease in H2 and will room revenue improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Most renovations are done apart from Bangalore (18 keys at a time). Management called better room revenue growth in H2 a very fair assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition appetite with ~₹1,000 cr cash and little FY28 addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to acquisitions, preferring brownfield or operating hotels for faster market entry, but gave no specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and value of Hyderabad land, Hebbal and Goa projects, and starting ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give land value, project costs or starting ARR for Hebbal and Goa, referring to stock exchange filings; said 10-year DCF, IRR and NPV analysis is done for each project.

qa_highlights.question: Wildflower Hall: when revenue booking starts and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue booking starts from end of Q4; management said the 47.1% revenue share to the state government is large and the aim is to make the hotel profitable.

risks_watch: Renovation-led inventory loss at Mumbai and Bangalore; Bangalore renovation still ongoing.
Dependence on foreign tourist recovery and geopolitical developments, which management flagged as the key swing factor.
Greenfield execution: Goa awaiting approvals, Tirupati delayed by land change, Hebbal capex undisclosed, Oberoi Grand heritage approvals.
Rajgarh remains reliant on air connectivity (only Delhi-Khajuraho flights); a Mumbai flight would help.
Management declined to disclose key capex and land-value figures, limiting visibility on cash deployment of ~₹1,100 cr+ reserves.
F&B growth not disclosed; analyst computed ~3% growth ex-OFS, which management did not confirm.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the Q3/Q4 outlook, but guarded on specifics: management declined to give project costs, land value, starting ARR, F&B growth and detailed opening dates, pointing to stock exchange filings instead.

Q2 was a good quarter for us and we achieved strong results in terms of ARR increase.
The market is strong and we're positive about Q3 and Q4 if there are no unknown events that happen globally.

adds.what: ~300-key Trident Hyderabad hotel (land ~10 acres freehold, planned)
Oberoi Grand heritage renovation with larger rooms and lower room count (inventory reduction, not an addition)
Hebbal Bangalore project: two hotels plus commercial/retail, ~1.7 million sq ft; ground-breaking early calendar 2027
Tirupati greenfield hotel (delayed due to land allocation change)
Hyderabad Raidurg Oberoi (management contract) and Trident Hi-Tech City hotel, to open within two-year window

growth.why: Management expects good Q3 and Q4 (conditional on no unknown global events) backed by rising foreign bookings and strong domestic demand, with revenue up 16% in Q2 and RevPAR up 18.3%; capacity adds are mostly long-dated (Hebbal ground-breaking CY2027, ~1,100 owned keys by 2030), and near-term room revenue growth depends on renovations finishing, not new capacity.

oneOffs.what: One-time settlement of prior-period lease rental at Oberoi Delhi, which raised Q2 finance cost (amount not disclosed)
Mumbai/Bangalore renovations cut inventory; occupancy 71% vs 72% last year on reported basis, a drag on volume rather than a base effect

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 16% against RevPAR up 18.3%, with RevPAR driven mainly by ARR (industry ARR +8-10%, occupancy +1-3%) while reported occupancy fell to 71% from 72% during renovations, so growth is price-led and recurring rather than volume-led. The only one-off the brief points to is a one-time prior-period lease settlement at Oberoi Delhi that inflated Q2 finance cost, which depresses PA

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA up 19% vs revenue up 16%, with RevPAR up 18.3% on ARR gains and Oberoi Rajgarh expected EBITDA-positive in Q3 after a negative Q1; the finance cost is a one-time lease settlement expected to normalise.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new owned keys are due in the window: Hebbal ground-breaking is CY2027, Tirupati is deferred, Goa awaits approvals, and the Hyderabad Trident (~300 keys) is only at land stage, so the near-term adds are minor.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupancy fell to 71% from 74% on Mumbai renovation inventory loss, but ~76% on reduced inventory and management expects better H2 room revenue growth as Mumbai and most renovations finish.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 71%, so there is no capacity pressure, but cash of over ₹1,100 cr and the ~1,100-key owned pipeline by 2030 mean further project disclosures (Hebbal costs, Hyderabad) are likely through filings, with the Hebbal ground-breaking in CY2027.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is positive on Q3 and Q4 with Q2 RevPAR up 18.3% and foreign bookings healthier, but the outlook is conditional on no unknown global events and no numeric guidance was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged foreign tourist recovery and geopolitics as the key swing factor, and the analyst flagged single-digit RevPAR growth in Bangalore and Chennai.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Oberoi Mumbai F&B/spa/gym reopens in January and the Wildflower Hall (Shimla) revenue booking starts at end of Q4, but no new brand or product launch with a date was given.

rows.label: Wildflower Hall (Shimla) revenue booking
rows.why: Contract revenue booking is expected from end of Q4, with the state government taking a 47.1% revenue share and the aim to make the hotel profitable.

rows.label: Mauritius and international recovery
rows.why: Mauritius occupancy rose to about 67% after UK travel restrictions lifted in early Q2, and management expects healthier foreign growth in Q3.

rows.label: Acquisition appetite with ~₹1,000 cr+ cash
rows.why: Management is open to acquisitions, preferring brownfield or operating hotels, but gave no specifics on size or timing with cash above ₹1,100 cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on ARR-led RevPAR, the Q3/Q4 outlook and foreign booking recovery, but guarded on project costs, land value, starting ARR, F&B growth and opening dates; analysts pressed on the revenue-RevPAR gap, the elevated finance cost, and cash deployment.
